newsitem.title: UK: Saracen says would consider new HSBC bid.
newsitem.headline: Saracen says would consider new HSBC bid.

text.p: Saracen Value Trust said on Friday it did not feel management takeover proposals by HSBC Asset Management took account of shareholder value, but would consider a new and improved bid from the group.

"The board and its advisers have considered your proposals at length and regret to inform you that they do not believe that your proposal addresses the issue of value for shareholders," Saracen chairman Antony Dick said in a letter to HSBC Asset Management chief investment officer Dean Buckley.
Buckley presented HSBC's proposals to Saracen on Monday.

Dick stated again that Saracen had received a number of approaches from other fund management groups, some of which involved a partial return of funds to shareholders. Invesco said earlier on Friday it may make a bid for Saracen.

Dick said that if HSBC came up with new proposals, "which might involve a return of capital to shareholders", it would be prepared to consider them in conjunction with the other offers it had received.
Saracen has said alternative solutions included a restructuring of the trust, returning cash to shareholders, or employing other managers.
HSBC Asset Management said last week it wanted to replace SFM Investment Management as the fund manager of the trust.
HSBC proposed to waive its management fee for the first two years of any contract and to reduce the notice period from two years to one year at the end of three years.
After two years HSBC would also reduce the management fee to 75 basis points (bps) from the current 100 bps of total assets less liabilities.
It said it had the support of shareholders representing 49.3 percent of Saracen's issued share capital.
Saracen's Dick said HSBC's proposals failed to clearly demonstrate how it could narrow Saracen's discount net asset value.
"Other aspects of your proposal that gave the directors cause for concern were the shortness of your smaller company unit trust track record and the relatively recent arrival of your team," he said.
Dick did say in the letter that recent feedback from shareholders indicated concerns about the high level of the discount to net asset value.
Saracen shares were quoted at 97 pence on Friday, up from 89 before HSBC's offer over a week ago, but still at a discount to its NAV of 109.82 pence per share.
Invesco Asset Management said on Friday it could bid for Saracen in the near future.
"Invesco may in the near future submit proposals to the board of Saracen which may or may not lead to an offer being made for the entire issued share capital of Saracen," Invesco said in a statement.
